text:
liam: Heads up — after yesterday's model bump (checkpoint v3.2.1 -> v3.3.0) staging p50 token latency jumped ~1.5x for long contexts. Rolling deploy stopped. :warning:
maya: saw that, traces look like kernel selector chose fallback_matmul path instead of fused_attention for many requests.
devin: reproducing locally with the new tokenizer config — note v3.3 flipped 'eos_token_id' from 2 -> 1 and max_position_embeddings bumped to 4096 in config.json. Could that change compiled kernel decision?
chen: interesting — kernel selection uses sequence length hist + model max_seq to pick block sizes. If max_position_embeddings increases, we may fall into different kernel thresholds.
liam: attaching a small perf snippet from staging:
```
req_id=abc123 p50=42ms p95=310ms model=v3.3.0 seq=2048 kernels=fallback_matmul
req_id=abc124 p50=28ms p95=120ms model=v3.2.1 seq=2048 kernels=fused_attn
```

maya: also noticed kvcache hit rate dropped by ~30% — seems prompts are being tokenized differently, more unique prefixes so cache keys miss.
devin: bisect started — suspect one of these commits: tokenizer normalizer change (r/infra/tokenizer: normalize-unicode), model config drift, or kernel threshold tweak in serving selector.
chen: quick experiment: pinned model config's max_position_embeddings back to 2048 locally, kernel selector picks fused_attn and latency normalizes. So config drift is likely.
maya: but why kvcache miss spike? tokenizer normalizer could change token boundaries -> different prefix hashes.
liam: agree. Plan: 1) revert model config bump on staging (keep v3.3 content but override max_pos), 2) run bisect on tokenizer normalizer commit, 3) add guard in selector to use observed seq distribution instead of config-only decision. Can we do the temporary revert now?
devin: started rollback on staging (rolling to v3.2.1 config overlay). infra-bot: deploy started
infra-bot: deploy job 9876 started -> staging-group-a
maya: perf after revert (after 10m): p50 back to 29ms, p95 down to 130ms. kvcache back to baseline. :tada:
chen: for next steps: add unit that computes observed seq_hist from recent 10k reqs and prefer it over model.max_pos when making kernel decisions. Also add test that tokenizer normalizer changes include fingerprint diff check to alert when cache keys may change.
liam: filed issues: PERF-1129 (selector fallback hardening), PERF-1130 (tokenizer-change alert). Assigning to devin/chen.
devin: will bisect tokenizer repo tomorrow, also adding a CI perf job to run small end-to-end tokenization hashcheck on PRs that touch tokenizer.
maya: thanks — leaving rollback in place until we have selector guard. Keeping this thread updated.
liam: thanks all, great triage. Closing status: rollout blocked -> mitigated by config overlay revert. last logs saved to s3://redwood-staging/perf/1792103456/
